findings.summary: The Materialized Views table contradicts the bullets on indexing and omits the key trade-off, so it is misleading.
findings.evidence: "Index | no | yes" versus "CONCURRENTLY needs a unique index"
findings.fix: Change the row to "Index | not on the view itself (indexes go on base tables) | can be indexed" or drop it.

findings.summary: Code is shown before its one-line idea in the View and Materialized View sections, and the bullet "Simple views are updatable" is placed under Gotchas without a rule for what counts as simple.
findings.evidence: "Replacement must keep existing column names and order (PostgreSQL)" then "sql CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v AS SELECT ...;"; "Simple views are updatable"
findings.fix: State the idea in a bullet immediately before each code block, and define 'simple' (single table, no aggregates, DISTINCT or GROUP BY).

findings.summary: The CONCAT bullet holds two ideas (PostgreSQL/SQL Server behaviour and MySQL behaviour), and the Remember note is a prose line.
findings.evidence: "CONCAT(a,b) treats NULL as empty in PostgreSQL and SQL Server; MySQL returns NULL"; "Substring positions start at 1, not 0. For NULLs, wrap values in COALESCE: MySQL's CONCAT returns NULL too."
findings.fix: Split the bullet per engine or use a small engine table, and turn the Remember note into two one-line bullets.

findings.summary: The code output is shown as bare lines (c, p, a, NULL) and is ambiguous about which engine produced it.
findings.evidence:
"c
p
a
NULL" after "SELECT CONCAT('a', NULL) AS c, 'a' || NULL AS p;"
findings.fix: Render it as a two-column result table and label it PostgreSQL.

findings.summary: The Slice and Search table lists POSITION but the INSTR equivalent is a loose bullet outside the table, and the LENGTH bullet has two ideas.
findings.evidence: "INSTR(s, 'x') is the same idea in other engines"; "LENGTH counts characters in PostgreSQL, bytes in some engines"
findings.fix: Add INSTR to the table's POSITION row and split the LENGTH bullet or name the engines.

findings.summary: The date and time bullets mix several ideas and the date-diff table lacks a rule for the date/timestamp subtraction types.
findings.evidence: "NOW() / CURRENT_TIMESTAMP return a timestamp with time zone" then "Both are fixed for the whole transaction"; "DATE_TRUNC('month', ts) rounds down to the period start; use it for monthly GROUP BY"
findings.fix: Split the DATE_TRUNC bullet into its rule and its use case, and put the engine name on the first PostgreSQL rows of the table.

findings.summary: The Remember callout 'Before arithmetic' is a fragment, and the CASE bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: "Simple CASE compares with = only, so it never matches NULL"; "Before arithmetic Wrap nullable columns: COALESCE(col, 0) + 1."
findings.fix: Split the bullet into the rule and the NULL consequence, and reword the callout as a full instruction.

findings.summary: The engine table for rounding and the CAST table contradict the claim about PostgreSQL ROUND and TRUNC, and the rounding section holds several ideas in one list.
findings.evidence: "CEIL goes up, FLOOR goes down" and "TRUNC cuts toward zero" as separate bullets; "ROUND(float, 2) may fail in PostgreSQL: cast to NUMERIC first"
findings.fix: Present ROUND, CEIL, FLOOR and TRUNC in one small table with an example each, and put the float ROUND caveat on its own bullet.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet's third bullet merges two unrelated ideas and the date/string section has no table header or grouping, so it is hard to skim.
findings.evidence: "CONCURRENTLY needs a unique index; replace keeps column order"; "EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ts), DATE_TRUNC('month', ts)"
findings.fix: Split the bullet, and use a Call | Rule table for the date lines like the string lines.
